analysis.title: Mind on the Market
key_insights: US, UK and Eurozone 10-year yields are near their highest levels in more than a decade and a half, and Japanese yields are at multi-decade highs.
The report attributes the yield rise to persistent inflation, resilient growth and rising government borrowing, which expands the global supply of sovereign debt.
Markets are pricing 2 additional 25 basis point Fed rate hikes over the next 12 months (CME Group, as of 11/4/2026). The authors expect rates to stay structurally higher than in the 2010s.
Debt-to-EBITDA by equity market: MSCI EM 1.88, S&P 500 1.90, MSCI Europe 2.82, MSCI Japan 3.34, Russell 2000 5.53 (FactSet, as of 10/30/2026).

MSCI EM debt-to-EBITDA fell from roughly 2.6x in June 2024 to 1.9x, in line with the S&P 500. The report ties the improvement to higher profitability and the growing weight of large AI-related technology companies in the index.
Small caps are the outlier on leverage and have thinner earnings cushions, which may explain why their performance relative to the S&P 500 has been sensitive to interest rates.

Over the past year, rising US 10-year yields have coincided with small-cap underperformance versus the S&P 500, most clearly in September and early October. The small-cap lead over large caps was fully erased in September and the Russell 2000 briefly trailed the S&P 500.

The authors expect markets with stronger profitability and more manageable debt to be better positioned if financing costs stay elevated. Rate-sensitive areas could benefit if yields fall, but the reason for the decline (lower inflation versus weaker growth) matters.

sector_views.rationale: Debt-to-EBITDA of 5.53 is the highest of the markets shown, and thinner earnings leave less cushion against higher financing costs. The report does not state a formal rating.

sector_views.rationale: Debt-to-EBITDA of about 1.9 is the lowest of the markets shown, so these markets are better placed to absorb higher borrowing costs. The report does not state a formal rating.

risk_factors: Higher financing costs hit leveraged companies, particularly small caps, hardest.
Heightened AI spending increases focus on corporate balance sheets.
Rising global government borrowing keeps the supply of sovereign debt high and yields elevated.
A yield decline driven by weaker growth would have different implications from one driven by moderating inflation.
